pages.api:
# API

> One JSON object per window on stdout. Spatial lines, when enabled, are a different sink and a different schema.

## Stdout report

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `status` | `no_source`, `no_frames`, `mov`, or `occ` |
| `source` | Device description, or null when the tty did not open |
| `simulated` | True only under `--simulate` |
| `kind` | `mov` or `occ` for the last accepted line in the window, else null |
| `distance_m` | Metres from that line, else null. Never a carried-over 0 |
| `frames` | Accepted lines still in the window |
| `mov_lines`, `occ_lines` | Counts of those lines in the window |
| `undecoded_lines`, `rejected_lines`, `resync_bytes` | Parser counters for the window |
| `checksum_errors` | Always 0. The manual defines no checksum |
| `window_s` | The interval or the `--once` window |
| `export` | `http://127.0.0.1:8054` when the bind succeeded, else null |
| `error` | A sentence naming the device, baud, and next check, else null |
| `timestamp` | Unix seconds |

There is no `heart_rate`, `breathing_rate`, `present`, `person`, or `track` field. `mov` and `occ` stay on this object. They are not promoted.

With the spatial feature, a refusal adds `spatial` (`no_pose` or `no_region`) and `reasons`. A line that is being written sets `spatial` to `emitting`.

## Export on 127.0.0.1:8054

| Path | Body |
|---|---|
| `GET /status` | The latest stdout object, or `{"status":"starting"}` |
| `GET /raw` | Recent distances: `{source, simulated, samples:[{t_ms, distance_m}]}` |
| `GET /guide` | `{"toml","pages"}` for this guide |
| `GET /healthz` | `{"ok":true}` |
| `GET /spatial` | Only with `spatial-evidence`. `application/x-ndjson` of `radar_range` lines |

## radar_range

Schema `spatial.evidence.v1`, type `radar_range`, frame `room_enu`. `position` is the antenna from `--radar-pose`. `range_m` is the module's `dis`. `fov_deg` is `[44, 44]`, from the manual's ±22° half-power angle read as a full beam. `targets` is 1 for one accepted line, not a person id. `uncertainty_m` defaults to 1.0 because the manual gives no sigma; override with `--spatial-uncertainty-m`. Proof is `MEASURED` for a real frame and `SYNTHETIC` under `--simulate`. Neither is ground truth.

No pose, no region, or no accepted line: no evidence line.

This cog does not emit SenML.
pages.glossary:
# Glossary

> Short names used by the manual, the report, and the spatial line.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mov` | Manual: a larger motion. Report status and `kind`. Not a person |
| `occ` | Manual: a still body or a small motion. Not a track |
| `dis` | Target distance in metres, approximate. Placeholder in the manual is `***` |
| breathing induction | The manual's name for the micro-motion method that sees a still person. Not a rate |
| `no_source` | The tty path did not open |
| `no_frames` | The tty opened and this window had no accepted line |
| `radar_range` | `spatial.evidence.v1` type for one distance along an unknown bearing inside the beam. Antenna position comes from the configured pose |
| `no_pose` | `--spatial-out` was set and `--radar-pose` was not. No evidence line is written |
| `source_id` | The installed object instance. Default `ld1125h-1`. Not the catalog module id and not a person |
| SYNTHETIC | Proof on lines produced by `--simulate`. Not a measurement |
| MEASURED | Proof on lines from an accepted UART frame. Still not ground truth: the manual calls the distance approximate, and this board is not yet tested |
| SenML | Not used. The manual does not define a non-spatial quantity for this cog to pack |
pages.mounting:
# Mounting

> The manual's two placements: horizontal, about 1 m, facing the radar; or hanging, about 3 m. Keep metal out of the beam.

Vendor install notes from application manual V1.2, not a measurement on this board:

- Horizontal: about 1 m, the person facing the antenna.
- Hanging: about 3 m. The manual's static coverage radius at that height is greater than 2 m.
- A person with their back to the radar is harder for the breathing-induction method to see.
- No metal in front of the antenna. A plastic housing of about 5–6 mm is the manual's housing note.
- Keep the antenna away from HVAC outlets and fans. Moving air and fans are motion the module can report.

The antenna face on the owner's board is the blue side with four gold patches. That description is the board, not a drawing in the manual.

Distance on the wire is approximate. The cog does not turn it into an east-north point. A `radar_range` line, when the spatial feature is on and a pose is set, puts the **antenna** at the configured room position and keeps `range_m` separate.

This cog has not been tested on a mounted module.
pages.parts:
# Parts

> The module, a ground wire, a 5 V wire, and one data wire from UTX into the Pi's RX. URX stays open.

| Part | Notes |
|---|---|
| HLK-LD1125H-24G | Blue PCB, about 31 × 16 mm on the owner's board. Four gold patches. Silk `90-00074`. Pins along the long edge, silk `5V G UR UT`. Board size and silk are from that board, not from a dimensioned drawing in manual V1.2 |
| Jumpers | Three. Red for 5 V, black for ground, green for data is a convention only |
| Seed header | Pi pin 2 (5 V), pin 6 (GND), pin 10 (RXD). See **Wiring** |
| 3.3 V USB-serial adapter | Preferred while `/dev/serial0` is the login console. Adapter TX listens to module UTX. Adapter RX stays off the module |

Manual pin names are VCC, GND, URX, UTX, 2 mm pitch. Silk `5V` is VCC, `G` is GND, `UR` is URX, `UT` is UTX.

The UART output is 3.3 V. Do not feed 5 V into a Pi GPIO pin. Power for the module may be 5 V on VCC; that is not the same net as the data pin.

No FCC or CE mark is stated in this manual.
pages.safety:
# Safety

> Not a medical device. Not a safety interlock. A distance line is not a person and not a cleared room.

`medical` is false in `guide.toml`. Breathing induction is how the module looks for a still body. This cog does not compute a breathing rate or a heart rate, and it does not emit a vital-sign record.

Do not use `no_frames` as proof that a space is empty. The manual says the module stops sending when it detects nothing. A disconnected UTX looks the same.

Do not use `mov` or `occ` as identification of a person. The words are the module's detection class for one approximate distance.

RF: the manual states 23.5–24.5 GHz. This guide does not add a regulatory approval the manual does not state.

Power: VCC may be 5 V. The data pin is 3.3 V UART. Do not connect pin 2 or pin 4 to a Pi GPIO pin. Do not connect Pi TX (pin 8) to URX while a getty owns the UART.

The export listens on loopback only. Do not publish port 8054 onto a LAN.
pages.sensor:
# The sensor

> Hi-Link HLK-LD1125H-24G, application manual V1.2 (2021-9-16). Decode only what that document defines. Hardware on this cog is not yet tested.

The part is a 24 GHz FMCW human-presence radar. The manual's detection method for a still person is breathing micro-motion ("breathing induction"). That phrase is the method. It is not a breaths-per-minute field and not a spatial vital-sign record. The module does not report a heart rate.

Vendor claims in that manual, not measurements made here:

| Fact | Manual |
|---|---|
| Band | 23.5–24.5 GHz FMCW |
| Detection (vendor) | about 4 m while meditating, about 8 m while exercising |
| Hanging height | 3 m, static coverage radius greater than 2 m |
| Supply | 3.3–5 V, about 80 mA typical |
| UART | 3.3 V, factory 115200 8N1, ASCII |
| Beam | antenna half-power angle ±22° horizontal and vertical |
| Distance | approximate. The manual prints `dis=***`, not a numeric example |

## The lines this cog accepts

Exactly `mov, dis=<decimal>` or `occ, dis=<decimal>`: lowercase, one space after the comma, no space around `=`. The decimal is digits with an optional fraction. `mov` is a larger motion. `occ` is a still body or a small motion. `dis` is metres.

The manual's asterisks are a placeholder. `mov, dis=***` is not a reading. Zero, a sign, an exponent, and values outside `(0, 100]` are refused. 100 m is this cog's refusal bound, not a datasheet maximum.

When the module detects nothing it stops sending. Silence is `no_frames`.

## What is not decoded

| Item | Why |
|---|---|
| `str` | Named in the `test_mode` prose. No byte layout in the manual. A suffix on a `dis` line is rejected |
| `rmax`, `mth*`, `save`, `get_all`, `test_mode` | Configuration the cog does not send. Command replies are undecoded text |
| Line terminator | Not specified for report lines. This parser assumes LF and strips a preceding CR |
| Report rate | The manual says the detection cycle is adaptive. No hertz figure is taken from it |
| Multiple targets | The manual's report text is singular. One accepted line is one distance |

Sibling modules (other LD11xx parts) are not this manual. Framing alone does not identify the part.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Install the binary, point it at a tty under `/dev`, and read one JSON line. Export stays on `127.0.0.1:8054`.

Replace `<seed>` with the appliance address. Do not put a real address, token, or tailnet name in this guide.

## No hardware

```bash
cog-ld1125h-radar --once --simulate
```

The simulator emits `mov, dis=1.25` and `occ, dis=0.75` through the real parser. The report has `"simulated": true`. That is not a measurement.

## One read, missing device

```bash
cog-ld1125h-radar --once --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

If the device cannot be opened, the process prints one `no_source` line and exits 0. `kind` and `distance_m` are null. The error names the device, the baud, and the next wiring check.

## Continuous

```bash
cog-ld1125h-radar --device /dev/ttyUSB0 --interval 1
```

`--interval` is seconds between reports (1–60, default 1). `--window` is the `--once` capture length (1–30, default 2). `--baud` defaults to 115200. The manual documents that rate. Another rate is an operator override, not a documented module setting.

A device path must be under `/dev/`, at most 128 characters, with no `..`. Anything else exits 2 and prints nothing on stdout.

## On a Seed

```bash
# after the arm binary is installed on the appliance
curl -X POST http://<seed>/api/v1/apps/ld1125h-radar/console \
  -d '{"command":"--once --simulate"}'
```

Console commands the manifest allows: `--help`, `--once`, `--once --simulate`.

The export binds `127.0.0.1:8054` before the sensor is opened. If that port is taken, export is disabled and the stdout report continues. There is no flag to bind `0.0.0.0`.

## Spatial evidence

The default build has no spatial flags. A build with `--features spatial-evidence` still emits nothing until `--spatial-out` is a file path or `export`.

```bash
cog-ld1125h-radar --device /dev/ttyUSB0 \
  --spatial-out /var/lib/ld1125h/evidence.jsonl \
  --radar-pose 0.1,1.83,1.0,0 \
  --spatial-region region/urth/meso/room
```

No pose writes no evidence line and sets `spatial` to `no_pose`. No region sets `no_region`. `--spatial-out export` with `--once` exits 2. `source_id` defaults to `ld1125h-1` and is the installed object, not a person and not the catalog type.

Accepted lines become `radar_range` only. Presence text is not `human_confirm` and not a track. This cog does not emit SenML: the manual's distance is spatial, and the manual does not define a separate non-spatial quantity.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Read Hi-Link HLK-LD1125H-24G ASCII distance lines on a Cognitum Seed. The module detects a still person by breathing micro-motion. This cog does not report a heart rate or a breathing rate.

The `ld1125h-radar` cog opens a 3.3 V UART, resyncs on text lines, and parses `mov, dis=<metres>` and `occ, dis=<metres>`. It never sends configuration. A quiet module is `no_frames`, not a measured empty room.

`mov` and `occ` are the module's words for a larger motion and for a still body or a small motion. They are not a person and not a track.

## The short path

1. **Get the parts.** The module, three jumpers, and either the Seed header or a 3.3 V USB-serial adapter. See **Parts**.
2. **Wire data one way.** Module UTX (silk `UT`) to Pi pin 10. Ground and 5 V as in **Wiring**. Leave URX unconnected.
3. **Try the software with no module.** `--once --simulate` feeds synthetic vendor-format lines through the real parser and labels the report simulated.
4. **Install on the Seed** and run `--once` against `/dev/ttyUSB0` or the header UART once the console is free. See **Set up**.
5. **Place it** with a clear view. See **Mounting**.

## How the data flows

```diagram
flow
```

The default build prints one JSON object per window on stdout and serves `GET /guide` on `127.0.0.1:8054`. A build with cargo feature `spatial-evidence` can also write `radar_range` lines, and only when `--spatial-out` is set. Those lines are a separate sink. They are not mixed into the stdout object.

## What you get

| Output | Where | Use |
|---|---|---|
| JSON report | stdout | `mov`, `occ`, or a named empty (`no_source`, `no_frames`), plus `distance_m` |
| Store vector, id 28 | `127.0.0.1:80` `/api/v1/store/ingest` | Only after an accepted line. Failure stays on stderr |
| Export | `http://127.0.0.1:8054` | `/status`, `/raw`, `/guide`, `/healthz` |

See **API** for every field. See **Safety** before treating a line as a person.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> `no_source` means the tty did not open. `no_frames` means it opened and no accepted line arrived. Silence is not an empty room.

| What you see | Next check |
|---|---|
| `no_source` | The path is under `/dev` and the adapter is plugged in. Error text names UTX to Pi pin 10, ground to pin 6, and 5 V from pin 2 |
| `no_frames`, `undecoded_lines` is 0 | The module stops sending when it detects nothing (manual V1.2). Confirm power, baud 115200, and that UTX (not URX) is on the Pi's RX |
| `no_frames`, `undecoded_lines` > 0 | Bytes arrived and were not `mov, dis=` or `occ, dis=`. Command replies and `str` suffixes are not readings |
| `rejected_lines` > 0 | The prefix matched and the distance was not a plain decimal in `(0, 100]`. `mov, dis=***` counts here |
| Another program holds the tty | Only one process can own `/dev/ttyUSB0` or the header UART |
| Export missing | Port 8054 was busy at start. Stdout still has the report. The bind is loopback only |
| Spatial file empty | No `--spatial-out`, no pose, no region, or the module sent no accepted line. The stdout `spatial` field says `no_pose` or `no_region` when that is the reason |

Do not send `rmax`, `mth1`, `save`, or `test_mode` from this cog. The manual's threshold commands disagree with each other (`mth1_mov` defaults versus the demo and `test_mode` prose). This decoder does not pick a winner.

`--simulate` is labelled simulated. It is not a hardware pass.
pages.wiring:
# Wiring

> Three wires. Module UTX to Pi pin 10. Leave URX unconnected so a getty cannot send commands. UART levels are 3.3 V.

Power the module from **pin 2 (5 V)**. The manual allows 3.3–5 V and the vendor debug diagram uses 5 V. About 80 mA typical is why pin 1 (3.3 V) is left alone. Never put 5 V on Pi GPIO.

## Find pin 1

```diagram
header
```

Hold the Seed with the 40-pin header along the top edge and the ports along the bottom, micro-SD at the left. Pin 1 (3.3 V) is the left pin of the inner row. The outer row is the even pins.

## The three wires

```diagram
wiring
```

| Module | Silk | Seed | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| VCC, pin 1 | `5V` | pin 2 (5 V) | supply |
| GND, pin 2 | `G` | pin 6 (GND) | common ground |
| UTX, pin 4 | `UT` | pin 10 (GPIO15 RXD) | module talks, Pi listens |
| URX, pin 3 | `UR` | not connected | Pi pin 8 is TX. A console can write `rmax`, `save`, or `test_mode` |

`/dev/serial0` is the Seed console until the owner frees it. Prefer a 3.3 V USB-serial adapter on `/dev/ttyUSB0`: adapter RX to module UTX, adapter ground to module ground, and do not connect adapter TX. The cog's default device is `/dev/ttyUSB0`.

The cog opens the tty read-write only so the baud can be set. It has no write path and does not send those commands.

## Pins to leave alone

| Pin | Why |
|---|---|
| 1 | 3.3 V rail |
| 4 | the other 5 V pin |
| 8 | GPIO14 TXD, the console transmit pin |

title = "HLK-LD1125H-24G presence radar on a Cognitum Seed"
sensor = "Hi-Link HLK-LD1125H-24G 24 GHz FMCW human-presence radar"
cog = "ld1125h-radar"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "sensor", "parts", "wiring", "mounting", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api", "safety", "glossary"]

[links]
seed_api = "setup"
cog_installed = "setup"
cog_running = "setup"

uart = "wiring"

board = "Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (Cognitum Seed)"

  { pin = 2, name = "5V", to = "module VCC (silk 5V)", color = "red" },
